responsibility: This module is GCC’s SPARC target backend and platform-configuration layer, responsible for turning GCC’s generic middle-end and RTL into correct SPARC assembly across 32-bit and 64-bit SPARC ABIs, processor generations, and operating systems. Its core is the common target implementation in sparc.cc/sparc.c, sparc.h, sparc.md, predicates.md, constraints.md, sync.md, sparc-modes.def, sparc.opt, and sparc-protos.h, which define SPARC-specific options, machine modes, operand legality, instruction patterns, atomics and memory barriers, ABI rules, register and addressing conventions, prologue/epilogue and call expansion, PIC/TLS handling, diagnostics, builtins, and assembler output. Around that core, the many cpu-specific .md files model scheduling and latency for processors such as SuperSPARC, UltraSPARC, Niagara, LEON, and M8 so generic SPARC instruction patterns can be costed and scheduled appropriately, while sparc-passes.def adds target erratum-handling passes. The OS and environment headers such as linux*.h, sol2.h, freebsd.h, openbsd64.h, netbsd-elf.h, sysv4.h, sp-elf.h, sp64-elf.h, rtemself.h, and vxworks.h adapt the backend to specific ELF, Solaris, BSD, embedded, and runtime conventions including multilib, long double size, linker and assembler specs, TLS defaults, and memory-model policy. Supporting files such as driver-sparc.cc, sparc-c.cc, sparc-d.cc, visintrin.h, and small config fragments for bi-arch, default64, TSO, and long-double selection connect the backend to driver native CPU detection, frontend target macros and D target info, and the public VIS intrinsic interface.
